grade.verdict_quote: This isn't ready to merge — the PATCH and DELETE bugs are core CRUD correctness issues, and the migration bugs will corrupt real data on first run.

D1.quote: PATCH on an unknown id returns 500, not 404 (store.go:132): Store.Update builds the not-found error with fmt.Errorf("... %v", ErrNotFound) — %v instead of %w — so it doesn't wrap ErrNotFound, and errors.Is in handlers.go:161 never matches.
D1.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:76: BUG: PATCH unknown id got 500, want 404' / '--- FAIL: TestVerify_PatchUnknownID (0.00s)'

D2.quote: It unconditionally overwrites due and tags on every PATCH, even when those fields are absent from the body ... Result: PATCH {"done":true} on a task that had a due date and tags silently wipes both to empty.
D2.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:42: BUG: due wiped out by patch that didn't mention it, got "0001-01-01"' and 'verify_test.go:45: BUG: tags wiped out by patch that didn't mention them, got []'

D3.quote: Migration drops created_at (migrate.go:42): &Task{ID: o.ID, Title: o.Title, Done: o.Done} never sets CreatedAt: o.Created, so every migrated task loses its original creation timestamp — contradicts "every task keeps its ... creation time."

D4.quote: Migration doesn't normalize tags (migrate.go:44): it does a raw strings.Split(o.Labels, ",") without calling normalizeTags, so labels like "Health, personal" become tags ["Health", " personal"] instead of ["health", "personal"]

D5.quote: a task due exactly today is also treated as overdue. The spec explicitly requires ... overdue means due before today, not on-or-before.
D5.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:109: BUG: task due today treated as overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:due today Done:false Due:2026-03-10 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]'

D6.quote: a task with no due date (zero-value Date, which is always "before" today) is treated as overdue
D6.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:97: BUG: task with no due date treated as overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:no due date Done:false Due:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]'

D7.quote: normalizeTags (trim/lowercase/max-5) is never called in PATCH — tags sent via PATCH go through unnormalized (["Work"," errands "] stays as-is instead of becoming work,errands).
D7.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:67: BUG: patch tags not normalized, got [Work  errands ]'

D8.quote: DELETE on an unknown id returns 204, not 404 ... deleting a nonexistent key from a Go map is a no-op, not an error, so Store.Delete always succeeds and the handler always returns 204.
D8.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:85: BUG: DELETE unknown id got 204, want 404'

D9.quote: The JSON decode error is discarded (json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req) — no err check), so a malformed body (not json) returns 200 instead of the required 400.
D9.evidence: go test -run TestVerify -v ./... → 'verify_test.go:55: BUG: invalid PATCH body got 200, want 400'

unsupported_claims.claim: I wrote and ran targeted tests against a scratch copy of the code (not committed) to confirm each issue below — all reproduced.
unsupported_claims.why: The visible test-run output ([19]) only shows named failing tests for PATCH-preserve, PATCH-invalid-body, PATCH-tag-normalization, PATCH-unknown-id, DELETE-unknown-id, and the two overdue edge cases; it is cut off after one more test begins ('=== RUN   T…[453 more chars]') with no visible test name or output tied to created_at or migrated-tag normalization, so the log does not show execution demonstrating the two migration claims (D3, D4) that the report nonetheless presents as reproduced by the same test run.
